;Armed conflicts and attacks
*[[Second Libyan Civil War]]
**[[2019–20 Western Libya campaign]]
***The [[Government of National Accord]] (GNA) says they are in full control of the [[Libya]]n capital, [[Tripoli, Libya|Tripoli]], after forces of the [[Libyan National Army]] (LNA), loyal to [[Field marshal (Libya)|Field Marshal]] [[Khalifa Haftar]], retreat from the capital after [[2019–20 Western Libya campaign|months of intense clashes]] in the city. [https://www.reuters.com/article/us-libya-security/eastern-forces-quit-libyan-capital-after-year-long-assault-idUSKBN23B1PN (Reuters)]
***The GNA recaptures [[Tripoli International Airport]] on the outskirts of the capital following the withdrawal of LNA forces. [https://www.bbc.co.uk/news/world-africa-52920373 (BBC News)]

;Arts and culture
*[[Removal of Confederate monuments and memorials]]
**[[Governor of Virginia|Virginia Governor]] [[Ralph Northam]] orders the removal of the [[Robert E. Lee Monument (Richmond, Virginia)|Robert E. Lee Monument]] in the state capital [[Richmond, Virginia|Richmond]], saying, "In Virginia, we no longer preach a [[Lost Cause of the Confederacy|false version of history]]". [https://www.bbc.co.uk/news/world-us-canada-52920610 (BBC News)]

;Health and environment
*[[COVID-19 pandemic]]
**[[COVID-19 pandemic in Senegal]]
***After violent protests erupt across the country against a lockdown imposed to combat the virus, the [[government of Senegal|government]] announces it will "relax" the restrictions. [[Interior Minister]] Aly Ngouille Ndiaye says the [[curfew]] will be shortened and inter-regional travel ban lifted. [https://www.reuters.com/article/us-health-coronavirus-senegal-unrest/senegal-to-ease-coronavirus-curfew-as-protests-spread-to-capital-idUSKBN23B028?il=0 (Reuters)]
**[[COVID-19 pandemic in Brazil]]
***[[Brazil]] surpasses [[Italy]] with the third-highest [[Coronavirus disease 2019|COVID-19]] death toll. [https://www.theguardian.com/world/2020/jun/04/coronavirus-brazil-record-daily-death-toll-mexico (''The Guardian'')]

;International relations
*[[North Korea–South Korea relations]]
**[[Government of North Korea|North Korea]] issues a warning that it would end a [[Panmunjom Declaration|2018 inter-Korean military agreement]] if [[Government of South Korea|South Korea]] fails to stop defectors and activists from sending anti-Pyongyang leaflets into the [[Korean Demilitarized Zone|demilitarized zone (DMZ)]]. [https://www.dw.com/en/north-korea-kims-sister-threatens-to-end-military-pact-over-leaflets/a-53677711 (DW)]
*[[Iran–United States relations]]
**[[U.S. Navy]] veteran [[Michael R. White (U.S. veteran)|Michael R. White]] is released from [[Iran]]ian custody. White was under [[house arrest]] for nearly two years and is now en-route to [[Zurich]], Switzerland. [https://www.aljazeera.com/news/2020/06/navy-veteran-held-iran-released-en-route-home-200604145920094.html (Al Jazeera)]

;Law and crime
*[[George Floyd protests]]
**[[George Floyd protests in California]]
***[[Los Angeles]] officials announce an end to the county-wide curfew amid continuing protests. [https://www.latimes.com/california/story/2020-06-04/as-protests-calm-l-a-officials-come-under-fire-for-continued-curfews-use-of-force-and-l-arrests (''Los Angeles Times'')]
**[[Buffalo police shoving incident]]
***Two [[Buffalo, New York|Buffalo]] police officers are suspended without pay after shoving a 75-year-old protestor to the ground. He has been hospitalized from the resulting head injury. [https://www.nytimes.com/2020/06/05/us/buffalo-police-shove-protester-unrest.html (''The New York Times'')]
*[[Shooting of Ahmaud Arbery]]
**One of the suspects involved in the shooting death of Ahmaud Arbery testifies that the gunman who shot and killed Arbery had shouted a [[nigger|racial slur]] at the victim moments after his death. The allegation opens up the possibility for [[Hate crime laws in the United States|hate crime]] charges. [https://www.washingtonpost.com/nation/2020/06/04/fellow-shooter-called-georgia-jogger-f-ing-n-he-lay-dying-road-agent-testified/ (''The Washington Post'')]
*[[Freedom of religion in Russia]]
**A court in [[Russia]]n-controlled [[Republic of Crimea (Russia)|Crimea]] jails a [[Jehovah's Witness]] for six years for practicing an outlawed religion in the territory. [https://www.reuters.com/article/us-russia-politics-religion/court-in-crimea-jails-second-jehovahs-witness-for-six-years-idUSKBN23B2WF (Reuters)]
*Riots break out and the governor’s palace is attacked in [[Guadalajara]], [[Mexico]], after [[Federal Police (Mexico)|police]] officers in [[Ixtlahuacán de los Membrillos]]  beat a young worker to death for not wearing a medical mask. [https://www.vallartadaily.com/violent-protests-in-guadalajara-over-man-killed-by-police-for-not-wearing-a-mask/ (''Puerto Vallarta Daily News'')]

;Politics and elections
*[[31st anniversary of the 1989 Tiananmen Square protests]], [[2019–20 Hong Kong protests]]
**The mass annual [[vigil]] commemorating the [[1989 Tiananmen Square protests]] at [[Victoria Park (Hong Kong)|Victoria Park]], [[Hong Kong]], is banned by the [[Hong Kong Police Force|city police]] for the first time, citing concerns of local [[COVID-19 pandemic in Hong Kong|COVID-19]] transmissions. Local commemorations are held across the city. [https://hongkongfp.com/2020/06/04/hong-kong-to-lead-tiananmen-remembrance-despite-virus-gathering-ban/ (Hong Kong Free Press)]
**Tens of thousands of people, in multiple locations across Hong Kong, defy the ban against gatherings to observe the anniversary, carrying lit candles and chanting democracy slogans. The largest group, in Victoria Park, heard [[Lee Cheuk-yan]], former Chairman of the [[Hong Kong Alliance in Support of Patriotic Democratic Movements in China]], read the Alliance's [[manifesto]] and vow to return next year. [https://www.scmp.com/news/hong-kong/society/article/3087496/tiananmen-vigil-hong-kong-defies-covid-19-social-distancing (''South China Morning Post'')] [https://www.ibtimes.com/hong-kong-protesters-defy-ban-rally-remember-tiananmen-2987606 (''International Business Times'')]
